# Paymux

> Paymux is a self-hosted payment hub that gives merchant applications one API for payments, refunds, subscriptions, invoices, payouts, and normalized webhooks across payment providers.

Paymux offers hosted, browser-resolved, and backend-resolved checkout. For no Paymux URL in the browser, set the App's `checkout_mode` to `provider_action`, resolve the action with the server SDK, and pass only that action to `executeCheckout` in the merchant UI. All flows use the same provider routing and signed app webhooks.

## Merchant integration

- [Complete coding-agent integration guide](/llms-full.txt): implementation sequence, security invariants, examples, and acceptance criteria.
- [JavaScript SDK guide](/docs/javascript-sdk): backend client, webhook verification, and merchant-site provider checkout.
- [Application integration guide](/docs/api): authentication, amounts, idempotency, errors, and retries.
- [Payments and routing](/docs/payments): payment states, checkout, routing, cancellation, and refunds.
- [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks): exact-byte verification, durable acknowledgement, deduplication, ordering, and replay.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@paymux-js/sdk): `@paymux-js/sdk`.
- [OpenAPI contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/velixio/paymux/main/docs/openapi.yaml): exact HTTP request and response fields.

## Critical integration rules

- Create payments on the merchant backend. Never expose a Paymux API key to browser code.
- Derive amounts, currency, and order ownership from trusted server-side data.
- Supply a stable, unique idempotency key for every mutation.
- In hosted or browser-resolved mode, return only the customer-specific `checkout_url` to its authenticated customer.
- In hosted or browser-resolved mode, store `checkout_url` as a short-lived server-side secret until payment expiry so the same payment can reopen after a retry; it cannot be recovered by retrieving the payment.
- For merchant-site checkout, call `checkout` from `@paymux-js/sdk/checkout`; do not recreate provider-specific browser integrations.
- Permit the Paymux checkout origin in the storefront's CSP `connect-src`, plus the selected provider's required hosts.
- Treat browser redirects and checkout events as interface signals, never proof of payment.
- Fulfil an order only after a verified `payment.succeeded` app webhook or an authenticated backend payment lookup.
- Verify app webhooks against the exact raw request bytes, then durably deduplicate the `webhook-id` header.
- Keep provider webhooks and Paymux app webhooks separate; they use different URLs and secrets.
